correctness.rationale: Fix the unnormalized zero coefficient to 1 after modulation and scaling. The fourth moment is coercive and strictly convex on the real affine space of complex signals because the Fourier map is injective and the function |w|^4 is strictly convex. Scalar multiplication of the field acts on each punctured line transitively, so uniqueness forces a constant there. For u_j=q*b_j and U=sum u_j, character orthogonality gives F=1-U+u_j on the punctured perpendicular line and 1-U elsewhere off zero. This uses the fact that a nonzero pairing with a line attains every field value, also for extension fields. Every such perpendicular branch has q-1 frequencies. The reduced fourth moment is invariant under any permutation of the u_j and conjugation, so uniqueness forces a common real value x. The derivative factors to (k-1)(1-(k-1)x)^3+(q+1-k)(1-k*x)^3=0. The stated solution gives levels s/d and -1/d and weighted moment 1+(q-1)*s^3/d^3. At k=1 the minimum is q on a modulated line indicator; at k=q+1 only the zero frequency remains at the optimum. The candidates actually attain the desired ratio (their other frequency levels have modulus at most 1), and strict convexity and undoing modulation classify all extremizers. The unitary scaling cancels in the ratio. The center/arm ratio follows from normalization and changes sign exactly as stated, including q=7 and q=8 for k=3. For fixed k>=2, d is asymptotic to k*s, giving the stated large-q constant. The blanket nontransitivity assertion in the prior-work discussion has an exception at q=2,k=2: the affine stabilizer of the omitted point permutes the other three. This is not an exception to the mathematical finding, which here correctly gives an indicator extremizer.
residual_risks: The frozen finite optimizer and random-signal counts were not independently replayed; they do not certify the infinite family or equality classification.

evidence: All-exponent coordinate-subgroup crosses specialize to equal additive F_q groups and exponent four, but have only two arms. Affine-transitive supports have scalar modulations of the indicator as their exact equality class; q=2,k=2 is one such case.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither hypothesis covers arbitrary proper higher pencils. General pencils can require a nonconstant, even negative, central weight; the more general support bound does not resolve the sharp value.

value.rationale: A sharp evaluation norm and all its extremizers are natural invariants of this simple family of synthesis supports. Proving that direction choices do not matter even when the supports need not be linearly equivalent, and exactly locating when an extremizer needs a negative central coefficient, adds content beyond solving the coordinate cross or testing indicators.
residual_risks: The result concerns concurrent linear pencils in two dimensions, not general line arrangements or restriction estimates.
